prerequisites: Having completed Industrial Automation I and Industrial Automation II from the second year of this Degree.
The student should have assimilated knowledge of digital electronics regarding combinational and sequential logic.
The student of this subject must also have knowledge of computer handling and technical specification software applications, as well as programming notions.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design industrial control and automation systems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the basis of general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: IEC 61131-3 standardized programming system for programmable logic controllers.
Design of logic control systems with programmable logic controllers.
Process control using programmable logic controllers.
The programmable logic controller and Industrial Communications.
teaching_methods: Distance learning in virtual classrooms using current technology
Participation of the Teaching Team, Tutor Professors, and all enrolled students.
Virtual course, using basic bibliography and complementary material.
Autonomous work with available exercises and self-assessment tests, under tutor supervision.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 80% from the Presence-based exam and 20% from the Continuous Assessment Tests (which include practical activities). To pass the course, a minimum of 5 points must be obtained between the Presence-based exam and the Continuous Assessment Tests. A grade lower than 3 in the February Presence-based exam means the course cannot be passed. This grading system applies to both February and September calls.
